newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends sharply lower led by funds.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends sharply lower led by funds.

text.p: COMEX copper futures ended sharply lower Thursday, led by fund liquidation of long positions, amid some COMEX/LME arbitrage activity, though underlying fundamentals remains positive, analysts said.
"The weakness spilled over from zinc and aluminium into the copper market led by fund activity and the near term lows may not be in yet," E.D. & F. Man trader, Fred Demler, said.
COMEX May copper ended down 4.75 cents at 106.95 cents a pound, after seeing intraday lows at 106.70, the lowest levels since mid-February.

On Monday May copper had failed to breach last week's highs at 113.20, and the momentum of the four month old rally had been weakening since, until the breach of two-week old support around 110.00 cents Thursday, resulted in heavy stop order execution, traders said.
In the latest CFTC data on March 25, funds were net long 12,339 contracts, while the residual "non-reportable" category, representing small speculators, was net long 7,959 lots.
May copper closed at 106.95 cents, just below its 55-day moving average Thursday, but near March's intra-month lows at 106.90, and so may find support around these levels, analysts said.
But a further decline to more significant support around 105.00 cents is a possibility, traders said.
The COMEX May/July backwardation eased further also to 2.15 cents from 3.00 cents at Wednesday's close, and the LME cash-to-three month spread slipped to around $33.00 a tonne.

But a 5,000-9,000 tonne fall in LME copper stocks is expected in Friday's inventory data, analyst said, and the low level of global refined copper stocks, combined with good demand in the U.S. housing and auto sectors were likely to limit the downside though, analysts said.
U.S. February housing completions rose 10.8 pct to an annual rate of 1.505 million units, the highest levels since January 1990.
